3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit and in written statement it has been stated that the suit land was a kachari ghar of the Ex-Jaminder and after abolition of the Jamindary system the kachari ghar developed upon the Government as vested property. In 1958 Government reconstructed Kachari ghar and since then is in possession of the same S.A. khatian has been wrongly prepared in the name of the plaintiff but R.S. record has been correctly recorded the name of .the Government on the suit land these defendant has mangoes, jackfruit and other fruits bearing trees. The suit land has been published in the name of the Government in Gazette notification as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 5. From the records I find that this suit was previously decreed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Naogaon. Against the said judgment and decree the defendant Government preferred Title Appeal No.91 of 1992. The then learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Naogaon by judgment and order dated 05.4.1994 allowed the appeal and send the suit back on remand for a fresh trial directing the defendant to amend their written statement specially making statement as to whether the suit land was acquired by the plaintiff through .oral gift or by written document. 

 6. After remand the defendant Government made amendment of its written statement in the light of the observations made by the Court of appeal below. 

 9. There are some interesting features in this Rule. Form a perusal of the record I find although the plaintiff filed a typed plaint but for the Government filed a printed written statement. From a perusal of this printed written statement I find that it fit for all kinds of suits and in paragraph 8 of the written statement there is blank space' Where the Government pleader by handwriting filled it up trying to make out a Case relating to instant suit. It just like fill up the blank by primary school students. It shows clear non-application of mind by the Government pleader in making out Government's case. This is how the valuable Government property handled by the Government pleaders. 

 10. From perusal of the judgment passed by the learned Assistant Judge dated 11.1.1992 I find that the government at that time took up a stands that the suit land is on previous dag No.766 which is present dag No.816 just beside dag No.142 where Puranpur Tahshil Office was situated earlier. This Tahsil Office having been dismantles by a storm. The Thasil Office of the Ex-Jaminder Was abolished' and the land consisting in previous dag No.766 and present dag No.840 were gifted to the government by its owner Sayed Ali Mridha out of his own initiative.- But the Government took up a total contradictory stand after the suit has been remanded by amending the written statements .and their case is now that the suit land case earlier kachrighar of the jaminder and after abolition of the Jamindery system. This kacharigahr was developed upon the Government in 1958 and after reconstructing the same, the government possessing the same. The S.A. record was wrongly prepared and on correction the present R.S. record has been prepared in the name of the government. The suit of the plaintiff is barred by limitation. The present stand of the' Government is barred by estoppel. Since the case make out through amended written statement is totally nullify the earlier statement of the Government it suffer from illegality as it improving' the Government case by making out a case malafide to destroy the evidences led by plaintiff. By amendment anything could be done as provided by law but a new case totally contradictory to the original case make out in the written statement cannot be introduced. 

 11. From perusal of the impugned judgment I find that the learned Subordinate Judge in reversing the judgment and order passed by the learned Assistant Judge did neither consider the evidences nor consider the documentary evidences. The learned Judge did not at all consider the exhibits filed by the parties. The learned Subordinate Judge consider only R.S. khatian which has been prepared in the name of the Government, The learned Subordinate Judge was of the opinion that only C.S. record do not confer title to the plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge also found that the plaintiff did not produce any rent receipts. The learned Subordinate Judge considered exhibit 5 which relating to S.A. khatian wherein the name of the plaintiff and her sister and name of her mother appeared. The learned Subordinate Judge came to the finding that Sayed Ali Mridha did not acquire the properties of S.A. khatian No.248 considering this khatians the learned Subordinate Judge was of the opinion that since in the S. A. khatian the names of other persons appeared along with Sayed Ali Mridha as such S.A. record in respect of previous dag No.766 was prepared wrongly in the name of the heirs of Sayed Ali Mridha, the leaned Subordinate Judge was also of the Opinion that this recording of the names of the heirs of Sayed Ali Mridha has no foundation. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the R.S. khatian found that it was published on 15.11.1969 i.e. 12 years prior of the claim of the plaintiff. Wherein this land has been recorded as kacharighar and from this, learned Subordinate Judge hold that the plaintiff failed to prove that she or her predecessor possessed the suit land. The learned Subordinate Judge relied of Register No. XVI-A dated 05.9.1960 which is a photo copy found existence of the Kacharighar in the suit land. 

 12. From a reading of the judgments of the Courts below I find that the GovernMent did not exhibited the documents relied by the learned Subordinate Judge. Which is not permissible in law. Documents not exhibited should be left out consideration but the learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of these papers, held that the Tahsil Office of Government was in the suit land before R.S. record. 

 13. On a perusal of the records I find that the plaintiff exhibited Amalnama dated 20.4.30 five. Jamindar's rent receipt, the information slip of R.S. field khatian No.298 of Manda Moujia, S.A khatian No.248 C.S. khatain Nos.246 and 247 deed No.3548 dated 20.4.1981 executed by Alea Begmh infavour of plaintiff and on perusal of these exhibits I find that the name of Sayed Ali Mridha appeared in C.S. Khatian No.246 and in S.A. khatain No.248 along with the name of the plaintiff her mother and sister name were recorded. From khatian No.298 I find the name of plaintiff her mother and sister name were recorded from khatian No.298 I find the name of plaintiff Noorjahan Khatun appeared with her mother and sister and the nature of the land as it is appeared is "vita' I also find from the Istefa Patra that Panu and Abdul Mondal surrendered their Possession infavour of Sayed All Mridha and in the lapshir I find previous dag No.766 and quantum of land is 42 decimals and the nature of land is 'vita' From the documents submitted by the Government I find memo. No.777 dated 23.5.1995 by which the mango of the Tahshil Office of Puranpur Union was put into, auction. I find from the R.S. khatian submitted by the Government, the name of the Government appeared in dag No.840 relating to Kachari Bari. But from S.A. record submitted by the Government I find the name of the petitioners appeared along with others from C.S. khatians No. 246 I find the name of the father of the petitioner as a superior landlord and also I find Panu Pramanik and Garu Mondal as possessor as korfa rayat. From Register No. XVI-A wherein I. find that Paranpur Tahsil Officer of Manda Police Station is at serial No.1 dated 05.9.1960.This document has been delivered by the learned Subordinate Judge as follows:- 

 15. I find that the Government took up specific case in the written statement i.e. the suit land was gifted to them by Sayed Ali Mridha the Government on advice of the Court of appeal below as the learned Subordinate Judge did when remanding the suit, giving specific direction to the Government to file amendment of the averments made in the written Statement filed a typed application without mentioning under what provision of law they filed this application wherein brought fact inconsistent with earlier statements. It is not whim or fancy of the Government of play toys with the Court and the Court is not obliged to search the sections or the orders of the Code to fit the application as desired by the Government: In the said application there is no prayer nor it state under what authority the Court is to accept this application. Be that as it may Government now take up a total contradictory stands which they took earlier to the effect that the kacharighar was of ex-jaminder without mentioning of which jaminder. After abolition of the jamindary system this Kachari Bari developed upon the Government in 1958. Government from its own pocket re-constructed this Kachari—hari and was in possession of the same. The averments being made topsy-turvy to the statements made in the original written statement it hit by the principles of estoppels and no reliance could be made on such inconsistent case of the Government. It is nowhere stated in the application that the Tahsil office was in this Kacharighar front before. From reading of this so called amendment petition I find that it is full of mistake and shows clear non-application of mind of the Government pleader. The learned Subordinate Judge took this so called amendment petition a sheet anchor of his judgment. Moreover I find that the learned judge nowhere advert the finding of the learned Assistant Judge as if the learned Subordinate Judge disposed of an original suit. On this background, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the Opposite Party-Government prayed for remand of the suit to enable the Government to exhibit the documents upon which the learned Subordinate Judge relied as I find on the facts of the given case no fruitful purpose will be served. 

 16. It is very painful to see the valuable Government properties have been put into care of novice Government pleaders; it is k not desirable from a Government pleader to file printed statement I do not find this printed written statement fit with the pleadings of the instant case. A written statement only had been denial of the plaint case line by line but also it placed the Court to the actual Government case. It requires special attention of a very sound lawyer to write out a proper written statement. The entire defendant case has been damaged by this printed written statement. Moreover the evidence adduced by the defendant Government spoils the remaining Government's case. I find that the written statement having not denied the plaint case, the plaint case stands admitted.
